resources.string: TheTower
Am I in a basement? How did I end up here?
I can\'t remember a thing.
Did I fall off the wagon again last night?
Looks like the only way out is through the elevator.
I need to take the elevator up to the first floor and figure out where I am.
What the...? Why is only one button working?
There\'s a slot for some kind of cards here. Those greedy suits didn\'t seriously monetize the elevator, did they?
Actually no, it doesn\'t look like a payment terminal.
I need to call someone.
Damn it! Phone\'s dead. Cheap piece of junk!
Better look around the basement — maybe I\'ll find something to help me get out or call for help.
Did someone actually lock me in here?
Is this some dumb prank from Steve? If so, he won\'t get away with just a black eye this time.
Nothing useful. Just some kid\'s geometry homework.
They locked this safe for a reason — there\'s something important in there.
But I\'m no thief. And I don\'t know the code anyway.
Ha. Haven\'t completely drunk my brain away yet.
But why would someone leave a hint for the safe combination? Bad memory?
Or maybe I\'m doing some kind of escape room?
Then why does my head hurt this badly and why can\'t I remember a thing?
There\'s some kind of plastic card in here.
All it has on it is the number 1.
Well, I only saw one place where it could be useful.
Looks like a reception desk. Am I in a hotel?
And whose bright idea was it to put me in a damn basement?
Though money has been pretty tight, so maybe it\'s for the best.
I should ask that nice lady how and when I got here.
Hello! How can I help you?
Good... day? What time is it, even?
Oh, it\'s you. I\'m sorry, I don\'t know your name — you never introduced yourself last night.
Are you feeling better?
I didn\'t introduce myself to such a lovely lady? That doesn\'t sound like me.
I\'m John. (At least I still remember my own name.)
My head is splitting. Could you tell me how I ended up here? I think those last few shots last night were a mistake.
Oh, you don\'t remember anything? If you were intoxicated last night, that would explain a lot.
We were already getting worried about you.
What does it explain? Who is "we"? Could you elaborate?
You burst into our hotel last night shouting from the moment you walked in. You were furious.
I could even say I saw a rage in your eyes.
Rage and desperation. I\'ve never seen that combination of emotions before.
You frightened the staff and the guests. We were about to call the police, but you suddenly fell ill and passed out.
Oh right — "we" means me and Pete, our security guard.
We decided you needed to rest, so we carried you to a bed.
We had no vacant rooms, so we put you on floor 0.
The basement.
Yes... But we didn\'t charge you anything.
And I don\'t think you came here to use our services anyway.
I\'m sorry for the scene I caused.
I don\'t know why I came here. Do you remember what I was trying to say?
"Saying" isn\'t quite the right word.
It was hard to make out. It was mostly insults.
But you were clearly accusing us of something.
And you kept mentioning someone named Sara. Asking where she was.
Sara? My daughter?
Oh God... Sara!
Do you know where she is?
John, please try to calm down. We don\'t want another incident.
Sara is a very common name. We\'ve certainly had several guests by that name recently.
Of course, we can\'t share information about them.
I\'m sorry. Is there anything else I can help you with?
Please understand, this is serious. My daughter went missing recently.
(How could I forget all that? Idiot! Although — that was probably the point when I walked into that bar last night.)
I know she was taken.
I was told she\'s being kept here.
I assure you, we have a sophisticated security system.
Anything illegal on these premises is out of the question. I guarantee it.
I\'ve already had a close look at your security system. (Stupid key card.)
You mentioned a guard — what was his name, Poll?
I need to speak with him.
Pete. He\'s on the third floor.
You\'re welcome to try talking to him, but fair warning — he has a... difficult personality.
Only he and his wife Jane have access cards.
Her station is one floor up.
Please, take this access card. I genuinely want to help.
Well, at least there\'s that. Thank you.
Oh, it\'s you again. Feeling any better? Have you found out anything about your daughter?
I know she is somewhere here.
What was that?!
Looks like Jane isn\'t here.
Jane must have gone to lunch.
There might be useful information on that computer.
Of course it\'s password protected.
How are these complicated logical chains popping into my dumb, still-throbbing head?
It\'s a strange feeling, like someone is pushing these thoughts into my mind.
Who are you? Where did you get that card?
Oh, it\'s you — the idiot who was screaming his head off last night. Sobered up yet?
(I\'d love to show him who the idiot is right now, but Pete needs to talk first.)
Yeah, I did have a bit too much to drink. I apologize for my behavior.
Right. Now go home and let me do my job.
Pete, I\'m completely... Look, I need your help. My daughter is missing, and I know she\'s in this building — on the 6th floor.
I really need an access card.
No way in hell am I giving you a card. So you can cause a scene up there too?
I\'d lose my job for something like that.
Could you at least check the cameras or the records to see how Sara got here?
I\'ll get you money and make it worth your while. Deal?
Man, I don\'t know anything about your daughter.
And I\'m too busy to dig through every file on that computer looking for "God knows what."
If she\'s here, she\'s here for a reason.
And I don\'t need your handouts. We\'re done.
I\'ve told you everything. Just leave me alone.
Hands off! Those clowns at the bakery already botched the sprinkles so bad they won\'t stick at all.
The last thing I need is you poking around in there.
Doesn\'t fit....
What the...?
Ugh, my head! Why does everything look so strange? I need to sleep.
No. Sara first.
Argh! It gets worse with every floor.
Is this place doing this to me, or have I completely lost it from the stress and the whiskey?
Good Lord! Is that a person sitting over there?
Hey there, friend. You doing alright?
Eh? What\'s supposed to be wrong with me, sonny? Standing here steady as a good anchor.
Well, you look... strange.
Bah, strange... It\'s the sea wind and the years that weather a man, not your little city strolls.
Old age or not, Uncle Bob can still outrow any young pup out there.
Alright, never mind.
Fair enough. Not every old net needs untangling.
Are you sure you don\'t need any help?
Why do you keep pestering me, for heaven\'s sake? I\'m not in a hurry for help — but talking about fishing, now that\'s a different story.
I\'ll pass.
Well, well... Turns out you\'re not completely green after all.
I\'d already written you off — thought, let him fumble around as long as he doesn\'t tangle my lines.
But you\'ve got a sharp eye.
You sorted the fish by type and rarity, didn\'t you? Not every fisherman would think of that.
So there\'s something to you after all. In that case — I\'ll pass on what I\'ve spent decades collecting.
I\'ll show you the route to the best spots, but listen well: break the order and you\'ll go home empty-handed.
Listen: Take the rifle, the fishing rod, and other gear from the house.
Go to the lookout tower, climb higher, and look around for game.
I often managed to catch a pair of deer off guard when they were calmly drinking water by the lake.
Need to catch some fish for fish soup. There’s a good spot by the river—I always have a boat ready there.
Then head south — I\'ve set up camp there.
Spend the night, take a break
In the morning, go to the cemetery and visit my mother.
Go far north, passing between the big lake and the mine.
When I reach the signpost, I’ll know I can head west without having to swim across the river.
Near an old archway—almost as old as I am—my journey ends.
Already forgot?
You\'re kidding me. What kind of chest is this?
Even if I had a key, where would I even put it?
No code input either.
I was just looking at the chest and it opened.
Something is definitely at work here. Or rather — someone.
Why didn\'t you open it for me sooner, mysterious force? Did you need time to figure things out too?
God, I\'ve really drunk myself into a state. Talking to some higher power now.
Finally, the last floor. Please, God, let Sara be up there.
Oh my God! Sarah! My daughter!
Are you okay?
She\'s breathing. Thank heavens.
She\'s just unconscious.
Why is my daughter in chains?
What is going on here?!
I\'ll get you out of here now, do you hear me?
Hold on a little, sunshine, Daddy\'s here.
Ugh, my head is pounding. Where am I?
It\'s pitch black in here! I need some light, or I\'ll definitely break something.
Where is that light coming from? Doesn\'t matter — now I can see the light switch.
I need to get to the first floor. There should be a way out there.
Who said you could touch someone else\'s computer?
Where do you think you\'re going? You think it\'s locked for no reason?
Need to find a key [TODO]
I should try that key on the vacuum.
Lock successfully copied
Nothing in the clipboard
Ñ�Ð¾Ð²Ð° Ð±Ñ�Ñ�ÐµÐ³Ð¾
Is anything changing?
I don\'t think there\'s anything for me to do here.
Maybe I should look around.
I should take a closer look at the safe and think it through.
I need to turn the light on somehow. Wish I had a flashlight right now.
Argh! Phone\'s dead. Otherwise I\'d just turn on the flashlight on my phone.
I can see a light switch. I think I can reach it.
Hmm... I should search the room — there might be something useful.
Those 4 shapes on the paper must be connected to the code for this lock somehow.
Interesting — each of those shapes has a different number of corners...
Right — a square has 4 corners, then an octagon and a triangle: 8 and 3, and finally a circle with no corners — 0.
I should try entering 4830. Some digits are worn off, but it\'s not hard to figure out.
I need to enter 5 letters. Have I seen a 5-letter word anywhere in this room?
Caesar eats caesar salad, and the word "lunch" is underlined... What could that mean?
The lock needs 5 letters, and "lunch" also has 5 letters. In the top right corner, a changes to b. Maybe there\'s some kind of cipher?
What if it\'s a Caesar cipher? Of course! How did I not see that.
The Caesar cipher. I remember passing notes in class encrypted that way back in school.
Even if the teacher caught us, she couldn\'t read them, because she didn\'t know we were simply shifting every letter one step to the right in the alphabet.
The word "lunch" is underlined — if you shift each letter one step right in the alphabet, you get "mvodi."
Let me think... What passwords do people usually set? Favorite movie? A hobby? Their mother\'s name?
What about a pet\'s name? Wonder what the computer owner\'s pet could have been called. Plenty of options.
Wait — I think I saw a photo with some dog in the drawer. I should at least try entering the name from its collar.
The short messages at the beginning and end give a clue about what James was trying to write.
From the messages, the characters seem to be shifted — but the Caesar cipher doesn\'t fit here...
Since James mixed up the keys when reassembling the keyboard, maybe I should look at the layout and find the pattern.
Aha! James just put each key one place to the left of where it should be. So "wjmmf" means "hello."
I found the pattern — but which word do I apply it to? Five letters again on the second lock?
It\'s weird, but I should try entering "lunch" in the second lock too — just with the new shift rule.
The result should be KYBXG.
I\'m no designer, but that ventilation grille really doesn\'t match the color scheme in here.
Maybe the computer can help me find something. How do I get the guard out of the way? Even just for a bit.
Looks like the guard is fond of his <u>coffee</u>. Or he has to drink it to stay <u>awake</u>.
The guard mentioned the sprinkles on the donuts won\'t stay on...
And in a very unusual shape at that.
Maybe I could try to make the sprinkles fall off the other donuts in the box too?
What a crazy idea — why am I even thinking this?
I can\'t shake this thought of shaking the box to watch the sprinkles fall off the other donuts. The guard won\'t even notice.
What am I afraid of? I just need to <u>literally shake my hands side to side</u>.
What could these numbers mean? Looks like some kind of order — but one donut is missing.
Right. The last donut is on the desk — the guard hasn\'t finished it yet. So I have all 6 numbered donuts now!
...And what am I supposed to do with that?
That combination lock on the cabinet. I\'ll try pressing its buttons in the same order as the donuts are numbered in the box by position.
God, what am I doing? But for my daughter, I\'m willing to try even the most absurd ideas.
The layout of these buttons reminds me of something...
Right — the donuts in the box are arranged the same way. What a funny coincidence.
Although, the more time I spend in this place, the more I feel like coincidences don\'t happen here...
I need access to the computer. The guard is in the way. I have sleeping pills. And the guard isn\'t watching his cup of coffee.
No. No, I can\'t — I need to push those thoughts away.
But do I have any other options?
There\'s a key on the robot vacuum. It might open that safe. How do I get this thing to come over here?
Looks like there\'s a manual control mode. But I have no idea how to navigate it!
If only I had some kind of map or floor plan to work with.
I think I saw a ventilation duct layout somewhere in the room. What if I guide the vacuum through the ducts and into this room?
Something important seems to be missing here.
I can\'t paste it — it must still need to be copied.
How am I supposed to copy lock.3d if I don\'t have access to the computer\'s files?
Copy the lock... Copy the lock... Hmm... What to do. Think, John, think.
How do people usually copy something?
They just select it and hit "copy" — but that\'s only on a computer. Argh. Why doesn\'t that work in real life?
Right now I\'d love to just walk up to the lock, <u>press and hold my finger on it</u> like I\'m selecting text on a smartphone, copy it, and paste it into the program.
I\'m getting distracted. Can\'t give up — I need to find a solution.
Interesting — this lock model has multiple layers. I can actually see its internals.
If I were a professional lockpick, this would be exactly what I\'d need.
Wow. First time I\'ve seen an adjustable key. Wonder what that\'s for.
Maybe I can adjust this key to fit the lock on the safe?
But I don\'t know what the pins on the key are supposed to look like.
How did I not think of this sooner? I can see the lock\'s internals through the program on the guard\'s computer.
I can adjust the pins on the key to match the grooves of the lock — then it should fit.
This arrangement of cells reminds me of something.
One, two, three... Eight by eight! Like a chessboard!
So I need to press only certain cells. On a chessboard, pieces stand on specific squares. Squares... squares... Maybe I should look at the cell again?
The cell with the crow says CAGE, and the chessboard has letters from A to H. I\'ll check which positions in those rows the pieces are in and replicate that layout on the wall mechanism.
From the pictures, this is a timeline showing the development of the universe from the very beginning to the present day.
There are also elements at the bottom — looks like they need to be placed in the correct time periods based on their content.
First came life in the form of microorganisms. It gradually evolved into dinosaurs, which went extinct long ago.
When humans appeared, they learned to make fire, then developed agriculture.
That image looks like the Great Wall of China — I think it comes next, before the Black Plague. After that should be the invention of the telephone, and then a World War I soldier.
That leaves the Moon landing and the invention of the internet — I think it\'s shown as a globe with a network. These happened around the same time, but the internet spread a bit later.
Maybe I should check the books with the switch in different positions. Just in case.
I keep having this nagging feeling that the content of the book with the gibberish has changed.
I\'ve seen symbols like these somewhere else in this room...
Right — the bookshelf! Now I know which books to check. I just need to match the symbols on the spines.
I\'ve seen something like this in a spy movie. The books will each contain a fragment of information. Once I collect them all, I can piece together the full sentence.
Interesting — why are these words highlighted? Could this be one of the pieces I need to assemble the full sentence?
Who puts hyperlinks in a printed book? I tap the link with my finger, but nothing happens. If only I had my phone...
Among the highlighted words (if you can call them that), one is different — it\'s blue.
Looks like its meaning is missing. Maybe it\'s in the source?
If I were looking up a word in the source, I\'d open the Second page first and look for the word that has noun and guts above it.
Ugh, feeling ill again — there\'s some voice in my head whispering fidorb, fidorb over and over. What does that even mean?
This is some kind of torture!

Maybe it\'s not torture — maybe it\'s another hint. And "fidorb" is the word I\'m looking for? But what does it mean? If it\'s just a string of letters, that book "for those who can see" might help — it had a decryption key in it.
This is probably another cipher. Who\'s playing games with me? What\'s the point of all this?
Interesting photos — and that one with the motorcycle is really strange.
It reminds me of something...
This looks like a QR code — the kind you scan with a phone app or online.
They usually contain some useful information.
If only I had my phone, I could test that theory.
Actually, in the book "for those who can see," there was a link with "ScanQR" in the URL.
Maybe it\'s one of those sites that decodes a QR code from a phone screenshot?
Argh! That voice again. "Tap", "Tap".
Tap what? Tap where?
Or is that another word?
Beautiful images — especially the third one.
I think if I squint, I can almost make out some text in one of them.
Yes — on the third image I can see the word "Floor".
This book covers important events in human history — but why is the year missing in the second paragraph?
I should figure out which year is missing from the text. From the description, it sounds like something Edison invented that produced sound.
If only I had internet right now...
I remember — Edison invented the phonograph in 1877!
I watched a documentary about it not long ago.
Not long ago... How long have I actually been in here?
I\'ve been looking for words, not numbers — so what do I need this date for? That other book had something about turning digits into a number. I should try that.
That book mentioned something about a digital root. As far as I remember, you add all the digits together and keep doing that with the result until you\'re left with a single digit.
Okay, let me apply the digital root to 1877. 1+8+7+7=23.
Then 2+3 = 5. So the answer is 5 — let\'s hope the word I\'m looking for is "five."
"Blue tooth" — what could that mean? Actually, that\'s just Bluetooth, like on a phone.
Bluetooth — like on a phone. Funny. I remember sharing music with friends over it as a kid.
I\'d love to turn on Bluetooth on my phone like the old days and swap some fun pictures, back when everything was still good.
Something seems to have changed on the fish. There\'s a sequence visible on it. It looks like "left-right..."
But how do I use it?
There\'s a mounted trophy on that wall. The way it stares at me is unsettling, even if it doesn\'t look realistic.
And those antlers sticking out left and right. Like it\'s alive.
Looks like these antlers can be pulled.
Hmm, nothing happens. Maybe I need a specific sequence?
Every time I approach the mount, the image of that fish on the wall pops into my head.
The scales show a clear sequence of directions: ₽₽₽
What if I pull the antlers in the same sequence as the scales on the fish?
Left, right₽₽₽
Looks like I can move the fish around. In what order should I hang them?
Will it do anything? Worth a try.
I saw a note with a list of fish species in a specific order. Maybe the fish hanging here are described in that note?
If I match the information from the note with what these fish look like, the order should be:
I could try to trace Bob\'s route using the note he gave me.
It\'d be great to do it detective-style — pin the spots on the map and connect them with string to find the pattern.
There\'s definitely one here. Nothing in this hotel is accidental.
I think I\'ve got it. If I mentally connect the dots, I get two numbers: 3 and 7.
That might be what I need. Now I just have to find where to enter it.
There’s some bell-shaped thing on it. Do I need to ring a bell to open it? But that weird guy is a fisherman, not a musician. There’s no bell here.
Maybe this symbol means something?
Most often I’ve seen that symbol in the context of notifications—on a smartphone, for example.
Am I supposed to get a notification on my phone, confirm it, and the chest will open?
But I still don’t have a working phone.
Even if I got a notification, how would I confirm it?
Usually you need a numeric code. Where did that old man hide it?
Maybe I should take a closer look at the map on the wall?
What a massive fish on that wall! I\'ll take a closer look.
That mounted trophy is getting to me more and more. Something is drawing me toward it.
Strange feeling. I\'ve never had OCD, but I really want to rearrange those fish on the rack.
That map on the wall seems to cover a specific area.
Bob probably spends a lot of time there and knows the best fishing spots in that region. I\'ll take a closer look.
What are these — second-grader problems?! How am I supposed to multiply colors?
Unless the colors are just labels. I think I’ve seen those shades on the four panels to the right.
It looks like each cell here is a clue for what to enter into the chain lock. It has exactly 5 dials.
The colors probably refer to the matching cell on the panels to the right.
For example, the green circle at the top would be the first cell in the green panel on the right. That’s 6.
The first row is simple. Just apply the arithmetic operations to the numbers in the corresponding cells on the right. 6×1−2=4.
The second row uses colors instead of numbers.
But I’m not supposed to use the circles themselves — I still need the values from the panels. Nice try.
So: take purple minus blue — that gives red. Add yellow and you get orange.
>In the third row, it looks like I need to draw a pattern. If I follow the instructions from the panels, it’s 2 up, 3 right.
Then blue corresponds to “1 down”, but it has a minus sign. Maybe that means “1 up”?
In the fourth row, the shapes from the panels are layered over each other at different angles.
First: “horizontally mirrored blue”. I guess I need the upside-down triangle.
Then red and a right angle. Maybe that half-square needs to be rotated by 90°.
Then green and sin(x) = −1. If I remember correctly, that’s 270°.
So I need to rotate that squiggle shaped like the letter J. Now I just have to overlay the resulting shapes.
In the last row, I need to combine objects. We’ve got wood and fabric. Out of the options on the lock, only a flag fits.
The defendant, John West, has been found guilty of unlawful entry into Saint Mary\'s medical facility on the night of September 14th to 15th.
According to case materials, the defendant forced his way into the building through a service entrance and moved between floors of the hospital.
Security cameras recorded the defendant entering patient wards, utility rooms, and staff areas.
The defendant broke into medication cabinets, disabled equipment, and took access cards from staff members.
Security guard Thomas Pitt attempted to stop the defendant.
The investigation determined that the defendant had mixed a lethal dose of potassium chloride into the employee\'s drink.
The guard died on the scene from the resulting cardiac arrest.
Receptionist Emily Carter suffered fatal injuries after a ceiling light fixture fell on her.
The investigation established that the mounting had been damaged by the defendant in order to obtain her access card.
Upon reaching the upper floor, the defendant entered the ward of his daughter — Sara West.
Sara West was undergoing intensive care. According to the physicians, chances of recovery remained.
The defendant disconnected the child from life support, resulting in the patient\'s death.
Throughout the investigation, the defendant claimed that his daughter had been kidnapped.
According to the defendant, the building appeared to him as a "hotel," and the girl was allegedly being held "in chains."
The defendant also states that a force "from above" was helping him through trials and showing him the way.
The court takes into account the results of the psychiatric evaluation.
The defendant has been found not guilty by reason of insanity at the time of the crime.
John West is to be committed to a closed psychiatric facility for mandatory treatment.
Court is adjourned.
Easy, John. Don\'t move.
You are participating in an experimental memory reconstruction program.
We observed your memories in real time.
Everything you saw... the hotel, the floors, the puzzles... we saw it along with you.
Now we are certain that you truly perceived everything that way.
No... It wasn\'t a dream...
His vitals are unstable.
Prepare the patient for the next stage.
What are you going to do to me?..
Further treatment will require direct intervention in brain activity.
No! Don\'t touch me!
Administer the sedative.
Wait!..

yes

Grammar of Chaos

The Library of Babel is a place for scholars, writers, and anyone seeking inspiration or pondering the peculiarities of existence. It contains every possible combination of letters, spaces, commas and periods — forming every book ever written and every book that could ever be written. Any page you find will exist in the same form and in the same place forever — for this infinite library already exists, simply waiting to be opened. This edition presents a fragment of one remarkable book from that very place. The full version can be found at:
https://libraryofbabel/interesting_book.
Chronicles of the Absurd

Once upon a time, a tiny hippopotamus named Jingle got a job at a library for earthworms.
 He diligently made sure every book was soaked in fresh carrot juice, because only then did the worms read with genuine enthusiasm.
 One day a crab in a top hat wandered into the library and demanded a novel about the adventures of a pair of slippers in Antarctica.
 Jingle nodded solemnly, handed the crab a pickled cucumber instead of a book, and announced: "True knowledge always tastes a little tangy!"

At the edge of town, right on the roof of an empty aquarium, lived Professor Keks — an owl who considered himself a distinguished expert in the philosophy of cacti.\n Every morning he put on his bright pink galoshes and gave lectures together with the receptionist in a starling house about the inner world of prickly plants.\n One day the professor got so inspired by the topic "The Cactus and Existential Longing" that he accidentally wrote his academic dissertation on a pancake and then spent\n three days chasing his own breakfast, trying to prove its scientific inadequacy.

A Book for Those Who Can See

Ciphers are everywhere — in text, sounds, images, and numbers. This book covers many different ways of hiding and revealing information, from ancient methods to modern ones. Symbol ciphers are among the most common: the simple Caesar cipher, the more complex Vigenère cipher, and digital codes like ASCII. Images can also carry hidden meaning — through pixel patterns or composition, for instance. Sounds are used in Morse code and other audio ciphers, where rhythm, duration, and frequency matter. Even numbers can be an encoded message: magic squares, sequences, checksums. A particular example is the digital root, in which a multi-digit number is reduced to a single digit that often conceals a pattern.

Those who wish to crack ciphers — researchers, cryptography enthusiasts, or simply curious minds — need a full set of tools. No Right to Duplicate

No Right to Duplicate is a visual manifesto from a gaze in love with reality. Every photograph in this collection is not the result of retouching, but a point where light, shadow, moment, and meaning converge. There are no tricks here — only observation, composition, and patience. The world in these frames is not beautified — it is simply seen differently. No filters, no post-processing. Just a lens, a point of view, and a little stubbornness. This is a book about how reality, if caught at the right moment, turns out to be stranger, subtler, and more poetic than any fantasy.
